title: DA: Errors in proposed farm-to-market roads coordinates already fixed
summary: The Department of Agriculture on Saturday said the incorrect coordinates of eight farm-to-market road projects included in its proposed 2027 budget were already rectified.

blocks.text: The Department of Agriculture (DA) on Saturday said the incorrect coordinates of eight farm-to-market road (FMR) projects included in its proposed 2027 budget were already rectified.

In an interview on Super Radyo dzBB, DA spokesperson Assistant Secretary Arnel de Mesa said the Agriculture Department had a meeting with People’s Budget Coalition, Better Gov. PH, and Bisto Proyekto to tackle supposed “encoding and geotagging errors” in the eight FMRs in question.
“The DA told them that we took responsibility and are already correcting those information and it was already fixed,” de Mesa said in a mix of Filipino and English.

During a hearing of the House agriculture and food committee on the government's response to El Niño, DA Assistant Secretary for Operations U-Nichols Manalo admitted that eight of 1,699 FMR projects under the agency’s proposed budget next year contained incorrect coordinates due to encoding errors.

This came after budget watchdog People’s Budget Coalition flagged provisions in the proposed 2027 national budget, which the House had approved on third and final reading, over allegedly incorrect project coordinates.
In an earlier statement, the DA said the discrepancies were traced to encoding and typographical errors.
De Mesa said the projects with wrong coordinates were less than 1% of the total 1,669 FMRs in the DA’s proposed budget in 2027.
The DA official said all of the proposed FMRs form part of the agency’s broader FMR Network Plan, which are already validated and geo-tagged. —KG, GMA News
